response.likely_cause: Severe reduction in image resolution, sharpness, and overall image quality from the clinic's camera setup led to significant distribution shift and increased referral scores.
evidence: High drift score of 0.99 across 50 scans in week 1 indicates images differ significantly from validation data.
Mean resolution dropped to 224.0 px compared to 1020.0 px in training (-78.1% relative change).
Mean sharpness fell to 0.000062 compared to 0.000399 in training (-84.4% relative change).
Mean quality score decreased to 0.106 compared to 0.5 in training (-78.9% relative change).
Mean brightness dropped to 0.294 compared to 0.373 (-21.1%) and contrast dropped to 0.0647 compared to 0.0963 (-32.8%).
Mean referral score rose to 0.354 compared to 0.193 (+83.9%), increasing the overall referral rate to 0.8 from 0.685 (+16.9%).
recommended_checks: Check fundus camera lens cleanliness, focus mechanisms, and lighting parameters at clinic IN-APT-01.
Audit the image export and saving pipeline to ensure full-resolution (1020.0 px) images are not being downsampled prior to model inference.
Re-train operator staff on proper patient positioning and image acquisition standards.
